query.name: Highest-Rated Movies by Budget
query.description: Identify movies that achieved the highest average rating relative to their budgets to determine which movies received high ratings having relatively small budgets.
query.sql: SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, m.budget, mr.avg_rating, (mr.avg_rating / m.budget) AS rating_budget_ration FROM movie m JOIN ( SELECT movie_id, AVG(rating) AS avg_rating FROM ratings GROUP BY movie_id ) mr -- movie_rating ON mr.movie_id = m.movie_id ;

query.name: Movie Count by Pairs of Actors
query.description: Identify pairs of actors who appeared together in the greatest amount of movies and rank the pairs by the number of movies they have shared.
query.sql: SELECT w1.worker_id AS actor1_id, w1.name AS actor1_name, w2.worker_id AS actor2_id, w2.name AS actor2_name, COUNT(*) AS num_shared_movies FROM playsIn pi1 JOIN playsIn pi2 ON pi1.movie_id = pi2.movie_id AND pi1.worker_id < pi2.worker_id JOIN worker w1 ON pi1.worker_id = w1.worker_id JOIN worker w2 ON pi2.worker_id = w2.worker_id GROUP BY pi1.worker_id, pi1.name, pi2.worker_id, pi2.name ORDER BY num_shared_movies DESC ;

query.name: Movies With Low Vote Count But High Ratings
query.description: Identify movies with low vote count whose average ratings are higher than the average rating of the movies in the same genre to find less widely rated movies that performed unusually well within their genres.
query.sql: SELECT m.movie_id, m.title, g.genre_name, m.vote_count AS movie_avg_vote_count, mr.avg_ratings AS movie_avg_rating, gs.avg_vote_count AS genre_avg_vote_count, gs.avg_ratings AS genre_avg_rating FROM movie m JOIN movie_genre mg -- 'tagged' in ER ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id JOIN genre g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id JOIN ( SELECT movie_id, AVG(rating) AS avg_ratings FROM rating GROUP BY movie_id ) mr -- movie rating JOIN ( SELECT mg.genre_id, AVG(m.vote_count) AS avg_vote_count, avg(r.rating) AS avg_ratings FROM movie m JOIN movie_genre mg -- 'tagged' in ER ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id JOIN rating r -- 'rated' in ER ON r.movie_id = m.movie_id GROUP BY mg.genre_id ) gs -- genre statistics WHERE m.vote_count < gs.avg_vote_count AND mr.avg_ratings > gs.avg_ratings ORDER BY m.vote_count ASC, mr.avg_ratings DESC ;

query.name: Most Profitable Movie Genres
query.description: Identify movie genres whose movies generate the greatest profit, where movie profit is calculated as revenue minus budget, to determine which genres tend to be the most financially successful.
query.sql: SELECT g.genre_id, g.genre_name, SUM(m.revenue - m.budget) AS total_profit FROM movies m JOIN movie_genre mg -- 'has' in ER ON m.movie_id = mg.movie_id JOIN genres g ON mg.genre_id = g.genre_id GROUP BY g.genre_id, g.genre_name ORDER BY total_profit DESC ;

query.name: Most Profitable Movie Production Companies
query.description: Identify production companies whose movies generate the greatest profit, where movie profit is calculated as revenue minus budget, to determine which companies have produced the most financially successful movies.
query.sql: SELECT pc.production_id, pc.company_name, SUM(m.revenue - m.budget) AS total_profit FROM movies m JOIN movie_company mc -- 'makes' in ER ON m.movie_id = mc.movie_id JOIN prod_companies pc -- 'Company' in ER ON mc.production_id = pc.production_id GROUP BY pc.production_id, pc.company_name ORDER BY total_profit DESC ;

query.name: Movie Language and Country Analysis
query.description: Identify the amount of movies from each country that include a specific language (movies are counted multiple times under different languages if they include multiple languages) and analyze how common certain languages are in movies from specific countries.
query.sql: SELECT c.country_name, l.name AS language_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.movie_id) AS total_movies FROM Movie m JOIN includes i ON m.movie_id = i.movie_id JOIN Country c ON i.iso = c.iso JOIN hasLanguage hl ON m.movie_id = hl.movie_id JOIN Language l ON hl.iso = l.iso GROUP BY c.country_name, l.name ORDER BY total_movies DESC ;

query.name: Workers Worked Both as Actors and Crew
query.description: Identify workers who have taken acting and non-acting jobs (such as writing or directing) in movies, with the name(or partial name) of the workers being provided by the user.
query.sql: SELECT DISTINCT w.id AS worker_id, w.name AS worker_name, p.character AS acting_role, wo.department AS crew_department wo.job AS crew_job FROM Worker w -- Pull acting roles (if any exist) LEFT JOIN playsIn p ON w.id = p.id -- Pull crew/non-acting jobs (if any exist) LEFT JOIN worksOn wo ON w.id = wo.id WHERE LOWER(w.name) LIKE COALESCE('%' + LOWER(?) + '%', '%') AND (p.id IS NOT NULL OR wo.id IS NOT NULL) --Ensures that they have at least one job and acting role ;

query.name: Keywords That Leads to High Movie Ratings
query.description: Identify which keywords lead to movies having good ratings by analyzing movies with certain keywords ratings.
query.sql: SELECT k.keyword_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_user_rating, COUNT(DISTINCT m.movie_id) AS movie_count FROM Keywords k JOIN taggedWith tw ON k.keyword_id = tw.keyword_id JOIN Movie m ON tw.movie_id = m.movie_id JOIN rated r ON m.movie_id = r.movie_id GROUP BY k.keyword_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT m.movie_id) >= 5 -- Filters out obscure one-off keywords ORDER BY average_user_rating DESC LIMIT 20 ;

query.name: Most Common Genre Pairs and Rating Analysis
query.description: Identify the most common pairs of genres that appear in the same movies and compare their average ratings to determine which pairs of genres receive higher ratings.
query.sql: SELECT g1.genre_name AS genre_1, g2.genre_name AS genre_2, COUNT(DISTINCT mg1.movie_id) AS movie_count, AVG(mr.avg_rating) AS avg_rating FROM movie_genre mg1 -- 'has' in ER JOIN movie_genre mg2 -- 'has' in ER ON mg1.movie_id = mg2.movie_id AND mg1.movie_id < mg2.movie_id JOIN genre g1 ON mg1.genre_id = g1.genre_id JOIN genre g2 ON mg2.genre_id = g2.genre_id JOIN ( SELECT movie_id, AVG(rating) AS avg_rating FROM rating GROUP BY movie_id ) mr -- movie rating ON mg1.movie_id = mr.movie_id GROUP BY g1.genre_id, g1.genre_name, g2.genre_id, g2.genre_name ORDER BY avg_rating DESC ;

query.name: Workers' Preferred Genres
query.description: Identify the preferences of directors and actors for specific movie genres by analyzing their distribution across these genres.

query.name: Most Frequently Occurring Movie Keywords in a Country
query.description: Identify the most frequently occurring movie keywords for a user-selected production country, ranked by the number of movies associated with each keyword.
query.sql: SELECT k.keyword_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.movie_id) AS movie_count FROM movie m JOIN includes i ON m.movie_id = i.movie_id JOIN productionCountry pc ON i.iso = pc.iso JOIN taggedWith tw ON m.movie_id = tw.movie_id JOIN keyword k ON tw.keyword_id = k.keyword_id WHERE LOWER(pc.country_name) = LOWER(?) GROUP BY k.keyword_id, k.keyword_name ORDER BY movie_count DESC ;

query.name: Highest-Rated Movie Keywords in a Country
query.description: Identify the highest-rated movie keywords in a user-selected production country by calculating the average TMDB user rating of movies associated with each keyword.
query.sql: SELECT k.keyword_name, AVG(m.vote_average) AS avg_rating, COUNT(DISTINCT m.movie_id) AS movie_count FROM movie m JOIN includes i ON m.movie_id = i.movie_id JOIN productionCountry pc ON i.iso = pc.iso JOIN taggedWith tw ON m.movie_id = tw.movie_id JOIN keyword k ON tw.keyword_id = k.keyword_id WHERE LOWER(pc.country_name) = LOWER(?) AND m.vote_count > 0 GROUP BY k.keyword_id, k.keyword_name ORDER BY avg_rating DESC, movie_count DESC ;

query.name: Keywords That Lead to Highest Average Revenue in a Country
query.description: Identify which movie keywords are associated with the highest average revenue in a user-selected production country.
query.sql: SELECT k.keyword_name, AVG(m.revenue) AS avg_revenue, SUM(m.revenue) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT m.movie_id) AS movie_count FROM movie m JOIN includes i ON m.movie_id = i.movie_id, JOIN productionCountry pc ON i.iso = pc.iso JOIN taggedWith tw ON m.movie_id = tw.movie_id JOIN keyword k ON tw.keyword_id = k.keyword_id WHERE LOWER(pc.country_name) = LOWER(?) GROUP BY k.keyword_id, k.keyword_name ORDER BY avg_revenue DESC ;

query.name: Actors Appeared Most Frequently in Each Movie Genre
query.description: Identify actors who have appeared in the greatest number of distinct movie genres, ranking them by their genre diversity.
query.sql: SELECT w.name AS actor_name, COUNT(DISTINCT h.genre_id) AS genre_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.movie_id) AS movie_count FROM worker w JOIN playsIn p ON w.id = p.id JOIN has h ON p.movie_id = h.movie_id GROUP BY w.id, w.name ORDER BY genre_count DESC, movie_count DESC ;

query.name: Crews and Casts by Movie Ratings
query.description: Identify crews/casts that have an average rating between [a, b] on movies they partake in and orders based on user-specified sorting order.

query.name: Actors by Movie Popularity
query.description: Find all actors that participated in movies that have a popularity value in between [a,b] and orders based on user-specified sorting order.
query.sql: SELECT A.id AS worker_id, AVG(M.popularity) AS avg_popularity FROM ( SELECT movie_id, popularity FROM Movie ) AS M JOIN ( SELECT id, movie_id FROM playsIn ) AS A ON M.movie_id = A.movie_id WHERE M.popularity >= ? AND M.popularity <= ? GROUP BY worker_id ORDER BY avg_popularity ? ;

query.name: Movie Ratings Within a Period of Time
query.description: Find movies that were released in between [a, b] and calculating the average of their ratings to determine whether movies within a specific time range has better ratings than other time ranges.
query.sql: SELECT AVG(rating) FROM ( SELECT movie_id, release_date FROM Movie ) AS M JOIN ( SELECT movie_id, rating FROM rated ) AS R ON M.movie_id = R.movie_id WHERE M.release_date >= ? AND M.release_date <= ? ;

query.name: Movies' Durations and Average Ratings Across Different Eras
query.description: Identify the relationship between movies' durations and average ratings across different release eras, and analyze whether movies from different periods have different rating trends within different duration ranges.
query.sql: SELECT FLOOR(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM m.release_date) / 10) * 10 AS release_era, CASE WHEN m.runtime <= 60 THEN 'short' WHEN m.runtime <= 120 THEN 'medium' WHEN m.runtime <= 180 THEN 'long' ELSE 'very long' END AS duration_length, COUNT(*) AS movie_count, AVG(mr.avg_rating) AS avg_rating FROM ( SELECT movie_id, AVG(r.rating) AS avg_rating FROM ratings -- 'rated' in ER GROUP BY movie_id ) mr -- movie rating JOIN movie m ON mr.movie_id = m.movie_id GROUP BY release_era, duration_length ORDER BY release_era, CASE duration_length WHEN 'short' THEN 1 WHEN 'medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'long' THEN 3 WHEN 'very long' THEN 4 END ;
